theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Energy (+2.90%) and Consumer Staples (+2.11%) led the market today, while Technology (-1.79%) and Health Care (-0.39%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.25% versus +0.46% for defensives and +1.08% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +0.10% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.25%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up +0.03%, outperforming large caps. The VIX rose 2.19% to 15.41, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold added 0.29% to $4,172.30, crude oil was little changed at $91.04, and bitcoin gained 0.16% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
